subject: RE: BrightEdge Health — finalizing DPA language for backup/DR carve-out
messages:
From: Sara Lin <sara.lin@brightedgehealth.com>
To: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: BrightEdge Health Legal <contracts@brightedgehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: BrightEdge Health DPA redline (backup/DR carve-out)

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Daniel and I reviewed the standard DPA and have attached a redline with a requested carve-out around backups and disaster recovery. Our security team is generally comfortable with Redwood’s controls, but they need explicit language that allows BrightEdge to enforce a 180-day backup retention window for our regulated datasets in the event of a provider-initiated restore.

Key asks in the redline:
- A carve-out permitting customer-directed restores from backups for up to 180 days after deletion for regulatory audits.
- Confirmation that backups are encrypted at rest and keys are customer-segregable (KMS).
- Process for notifying BrightEdge within 48 hours of any DR-related data access.

Attached: BEH_DPA_redline_v3.docx and SOC2_Type2_Q2_2026.pdf.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept the carve-out or propose language that preserves your operational recovery SLA? If needed, we can route this via DocuSign for signature once terms are agreed.

Best,
Sara
Sara Lin
Head of Security Programs | BrightEdge Health
From: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Lin <sara.lin@brightedgehealth.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Oct 2026 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: BrightEdge Health DPA redline (backup/DR carve-out)

Sara — thanks for the clear summary and the redline. I’ve looped in Rishi (platform security lead) and Lauren (sales operations) to help scope the technical and contractual impact. High-level: we want to be cooperative on audit and restore requirements but need to limit operational exposure that could conflict with our shared-responsibility backups and multi-tenant recovery plans.

Proposed next steps:
1) Rishi to confirm technical feasibility for a 180-day customer-directed restore and whether we can support customer-managed KMS for those backups.
2) We’ll propose alternate clause language that:
   - Allows customer-directed restores from snapshots/backups for up to 90 days as a baseline, with a possible exception to 180 days for verified regulatory audit requests (subject to escalation/approval).
   - Requires Customer to submit formal audit requests with scope and timeline; Redwood will scope and respond within 5 business days.
3) If language is acceptable, Lauren will prepare a DocuSign envelope with the redline incorporated for execution.

I’ll wait for Rishi’s take and circle back.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sara Lin <sara.lin@brightedgehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Oct 2026 11:38:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: BrightEdge Health DPA redline (backup/DR carve-out)

Markus / team,

Technical note from platform/security:
- Backups: We maintain incremental encrypted snapshots for multi-tenant pools. Snapshots are encrypted at rest; we can integrate with customer KMS for dedicated clusters (Redwood Dedicated / Private) but not for shared hosted customers without a dedicated tenancy.
- Restore window: Operationally we can retain snapshots for up to 365 days in our cold storage. However, enabling customer-directed restores beyond 90 days for hosted customers requires an escalation to infra ops due to runbook and capacity planning impacts (we currently assume most restores are within 30 days).
- Audit access: We can implement a 48-hour notification SLA for DR events and provide a signed attestation for any customer-directed restore.

Suggested contractual position to preserve ops flexibility: allow customer-directed restores up to 90 days; permit an exception to 180 days on a case-by-case basis where BrightEdge provides regulatory justification and pays a nominal restore fee to cover operational overhead. For Dedicated/Private deployments we can offer full KMS segregation and a firmer 180-day restore commitment.

I’ll draft suggested contract text for review.

— Rishi
Director, Platform Security
From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Lin <sara.lin@brightedgehealth.com>, markus_klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 08:25:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: BrightEdge Health DPA redline (backup/DR carve-out)

Sara — quick commercial note from procurement side: BrightEdge’s ask for 180 days is reasonable but procurement has a standing policy that any carve-out extending retention/recovery obligations beyond standard SLOs requires VP-level sign-off (our side) and may trigger a one-time onboarding fee if it increases storage or engineering support.

If BrightEdge is open to the approach Rishi suggested (90 days baseline; 180 days with justification + restore fee), we can move to DocuSign quickly. I’ll attach the suggested redline language and a short summary of the fee schedule.

Attachments: proposed_DPA_backup_clause.txt (inline in the DocuSign envelope if accepted).

Thanks — Lauren
Senior Contracts Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@brightedgehealth.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, markus_klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sara Lin <sara.lin@brightedgehealth.com>, BrightEdge Health Legal <contracts@brightedgehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:06:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: BrightEdge Health DPA redline (backup/DR carve-out)

Thanks all — internal check completed on our side. A few clarifications from BrightEdge Legal:
- The regulatory exceptions that would justify a 180-day restore are limited and will require a compliance case reference (ticket number or regulator notice).
- BrightEdge prefers language that requires Redwood to retain a tamper-evident chain of custody for any restored artifacts used for regulatory review.

We’re fine to accept the 90-day baseline + 180-day exception with a nominal restore fee and the chain-of-custody attestation. Can you please supply the revised clause and the DocuSign envelope so we can route to our Legal and compliance approvers?

Daniel Park
Director, Product Operations | BrightEdge Health
From: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Lin <sara.lin@brightedgehealth.com>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@brightedgehealth.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 15:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Final language and DocuSign for BrightEdge — backup/DR carve-out

Sara / Daniel — thanks for the quick turnaround and the flexibility. Attached is the redline with the agreed language (we incorporated Rishi’s attestation and Lauren’s fee note). Key points in the revised clause:

- Baseline: Customer-directed restores can be requested for retention artifacts up to 90 days after deletion without additional fees.
- Exception path: For regulatory audits requiring up to 180 days, Customer must provide written justification and case reference; Redwood will approve exceptions within 5 business days and a one-time restore fee will apply to cover operational costs.
- Security: Backups are encrypted at rest; Dedicated/Private customers can use customer-managed KMS. We will provide a chain-of-custody attestation for any artifacts extracted for regulatory review.
- Notification: Redwood will notify Customer within 48 hours of any DR event or restore activity affecting Customer data.

DocuSign envelope: https://app.docusign.com/envelope/view?envelopeId=87654 (DocuSign-envelope-87654.pdf attached for your records).

If this matches your expectations, please sign via DocuSign and we’ll process the exception workflows on our side if the 180-day route is requested.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this across the finish line.

Markus Klein
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference
Attachments: BEH_DPA_redline_v3.docx; SOC2_Type2_Q2_2026.pdf; DocuSign-envelope-87654.pdf
